title: Nurturing and Sustaining Long-Term Relationships
coreMove: Keep a bond durable by making reciprocity, maintenance, and early repair visible after closeness already exists.
sourcePressure: The ch07 source is narrower and stresses maintenance, reciprocity, and repair. It warns that close relationships erode when care becomes assumed, one-sided, or delayed until crisis.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Thinking a strong bond runs on history, loyalty, or familiarity without current upkeep.

sourceAnchors.name: relationship maintenance
sourceAnchors.detail: The ch07 source sidecar says long-term relationships need repeated maintenance after closeness forms.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A bond can keep its name while losing its current care; maintenance is how the relationship stays present tense.

sourceAnchors.name: repair before distance hardens
sourceAnchors.detail: The sidecar says repair matters when distance or strain appears and must happen before drift becomes structure.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Repair works best while the distance is still soft enough to answer.

hook: Do not take people for granted

exampleSpecs.domain: a volunteer search-and-rescue unit where two longtime partners stop checking each other gear
exampleSpecs.audience: a unit captain seeing familiarity replace maintenance
exampleSpecs.stakes: one missed battery check could cost a night search
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the captain reinstates a mutual gear check and watches irritation turn into relief when one dead headlamp is found before deployment
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a headlamp beam flickers against wet gravel

exampleSpecs.domain: a university alumni scholarship committee with lopsided follow-through
exampleSpecs.audience: a committee chair protecting a long-running partnership
exampleSpecs.stakes: donor deadlines will be missed if one member keeps carrying the invisible work
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the chair traces the drift through unanswered task notes and asks each person to return one piece of effort before resentment hardens
exampleSpecs.firstImage: sticky flags bristle from a stack of scholarship files

exampleSpecs.domain: a sibling pair managing care for an aging parent from different cities
exampleSpecs.audience: an adult child who confuses family history with current reciprocity
exampleSpecs.stakes: unspoken strain could rupture the care plan
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "I know we both love her, and the calls are not landing evenly," Hannah says, naming the maintenance gap before blame takes over

exampleSpecs.domain: a chamber-music quartet after ten years together
exampleSpecs.audience: a first violinist who assumes history will carry rehearsals
exampleSpecs.stakes: a festival audition will expose quiet resentment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: it takes Margaux one brittle rehearsal to see that shared history stopped replacing prompt apology and rotated administrative work
exampleSpecs.firstImage: rosin dust on a black rehearsal folder

exampleSpecs.domain: a co-op bakery partnership after the first profitable year
exampleSpecs.audience: partners who built closeness under pressure but now need upkeep
exampleSpecs.stakes: one partner is doing all supplier calls and slowly detaching
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 5:22 a.m., Michael decides whether to defend his long hours or move two supplier calls back onto his own list
exampleSpecs.firstImage: flour handprints across a steel prep table

exampleSpecs.domain: a neighborhood mutual-aid freezer program entering its third winter
exampleSpecs.audience: a coordinator maintaining trust after early enthusiasm fades
exampleSpecs.stakes: missed restocks mean families arrive to empty shelves
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: you stop praising the founding story and ask who checked the freezer this week, making current care visible again
exampleSpecs.firstImage: frost around a handwritten freezer inventory sheet

skillTargets: distinguish durable maintenance from sentimental history
choose early repair over dramatic confrontation
evaluate whether a bond is current or only familiar

tryThisNowSpec: Name one relationship that is running on history; make one current act of reciprocity or repair visible within the next day.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
